title: Tilt: a project saved after an angle edit by a build with defect #2599 keeps basis 0 with the new angles

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

PR #2730 fixed #2599: `EditOperationParams` now moves a tilt with `basis_version` 0 to basis 1 when the A or B angle changes.

A project file can hold the defect already. The sequence is:

1. A build before the tilt basis change saved the project. Its tilts have no `basis_version` key, so they load as basis 0.
2. A build with defect #2599 opened the project. The user changed a tilt angle, for example to A0 B180 or A180.
3. That build saved the project with `basis_version: 0` and the new angles.

A build with the fix opens this file and keeps basis 0, because no angle changes in that session. The operation posts with the cut plane turned, as in #2599.

## Source

The read-only second review of PR #2730 found this group of files. The review did not build and did not make such a file. The decision entry `docs/decisions/2599-a180-legacy-basis.md` does not name this group.

## What is not known

- Whether a file can show that it has this state. A basis 0 tilt that was not edited is legal and must keep its output.
- Whether the preview and the post agree for such a file. The review says that they agree, from a reading of the code only.

## What should happen

Decide one of these and record the decision:

- The application finds such a file at load and tells the user, if a safe test exists.
- The release notes name the limit and the manual repair: change the tilt angle and change it back.

Do not migrate all basis 0 tilts at load. That changes the output of legal old projects.

Refs #2599
